'''Austin Tyler Reaves''' (born May 29, 1998) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Wichita State Shockers men's basketball|Wichita State Shockers]] and the [[Oklahoma Sooners men's basketball|Oklahoma Sooners]]. Reaves joined the Lakers as an [[List of undrafted NBA players|undrafted free agent]].

==Early life==
Reaves attended [[Cedar Ridge High School (Arkansas)|Cedar Ridge High School]] in [[Newark, Arkansas]]. He won back-to-back Class 2A state titles in his first two years.<ref>{{cite web |last=Taylor |first=Erick |title=Reaves establishes mindset for scoring |url=https://www.arkansasonline.com/news/2016/mar/12/reaves-establishes-mindset-for-scoring-/ |website=[[Arkansas Democrat-Gazette]] |access-date=November 10, 2020 |date=March 12, 2016}}</ref> Reaves scored 73 points in a triple-overtime win over [[Forrest City High School]].<ref name="pflugradt">{{cite web |last=Pflugradt |first=Evan |title=Meet Austin Reaves: The freshman who 'catches a lot of people off guard' |url=https://thesunflower.com/11639/special-editions/meet-austin-reaves-the-freshman-who-catches-a-lot-of-people-off-guard/ |website=The Sunflower |access-date=November 10, 2020 |date=November 15, 2016}}</ref> As a senior, he averaged 32.5 points, 8.8 rebounds and 5.1 assists per game, leading his team to a Class 3A state title.<ref>{{cite web |last=Suellentrop |first=Paul |title=Arkansas guard Austin Reaves made team chemistry a priority |url=https://www.kansas.com/sports/college/wichita-state/article71426702.html |website=[[The Wichita Eagle]] |access-date=November 10, 2020 |date=April 12, 2016}}</ref> Reaves was named MVP of the state tournament after averaging 43.3 points through four games.<ref>{{cite web |date=December 27, 2016 |title=College BB: Former Wildkat's son plays for Wichita State |url=https://www.kokomotribune.com/sports/college-bb-former-wildkat-s-son-plays-for-wichita-state/article_d2707f3e-cbeb-11e6-ada9-0f245acf888a.html |access-date=November 10, 2020 |website=[[Kokomo Tribune]]}}</ref> He was a two-time Class 3A All-State selection.<ref>{{cite web |last=Suellentrop |first=Paul |title=Arkansas guard Austin Reaves signs with Wichita State's basketball team |url=https://www.kansas.com/sports/college/wichita-state/article71633647.html |website=[[The Wichita Eagle]] |access-date=November 10, 2020 |date=April 13, 2016}}</ref> On January 20, 2016, he committed to playing college basketball for [[Wichita State Shockers men's basketball|Wichita State]] over offers from [[South Dakota State Jackrabbits men's basketball|South Dakota State]] and [[Arkansas State Red Wolves men's basketball|Arkansas State]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Suellentrop |first=Paul |title=Arkansas guard Austin Reaves commits to Wichita State |url=https://www.kansas.com/sports/college/wichita-state/article55638735.html |website=[[The Wichita Eagle]] |access-date=November 10, 2020 |date=January 20, 2016}}</ref>

His older brother, Spencer, plays basketball in the top German team in [[EuroBasket]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Eurobasket |title=Spencer Reaves, Basketball Player, News, Stats - Eurobasket |url=https://basketball.eurobasket.com/player/Spencer-Reaves/347511 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250810042609/https://basketball.eurobasket.com/player/Spencer-Reaves/347511 |archive-date=2025-08-10 |access-date=2026-07-18 |website=Eurobasket LLC}}</ref>

==College career==

===Wichita State===
Entering his freshman season at Wichita State, Reaves underwent surgery to repair a torn [[Glenoid labrum|labrum]] in his left shoulder. He had been playing through the injury since his junior year of high school.<ref name="shoulder">{{cite web |last=Funschelle |first=Aliyah |title=Austin Reaves fights nagging shoulder injury |url=https://thesunflower.com/18856/sports/austin-reaves-fights-nagging-shoulder-injury/ |website=The Sunflower |access-date=November 10, 2020 |date=August 11, 2017}}</ref> As a freshman, he averaged 4.1 points per game in a reserve role. After the season, Reaves underwent surgery to repair a torn labrum in his right shoulder, which had dislocated three times during his college career, causing him to miss games.<ref>{{cite web |last=Suellentrop |first=Paul |title=Wichita State's Austin Reaves has shoulder surgery |url=https://www.kansas.com/sports/college/wichita-state/article142864384.html |website=[[The Wichita Eagle]] |access-date=November 10, 2020 |date=April 5, 2017}}</ref> On January 28, 2018, he posted a sophomore season-high 23 points and four assists in a 90–71 win over [[Tulsa Golden Hurricane men's basketball|Tulsa]]. Reaves made seven three-pointers in the first half, the most in a half in program history.<ref>{{cite web |last=Eldridge |first=Taylor |title=Austin Reaves' mother on son's historic performance: 'I was shaking' |url=https://www.kansas.com/sports/college/wichita-state/article197178404.html |website=[[The Wichita Eagle]] |access-date=November 10, 2020 |date=January 29, 2018}}</ref> As a sophomore, he averaged 8.1 points and 3.1 rebounds per game, shooting 42.5 percent from three-point range.<ref>{{cite web |last=Bitterman |first=Abby |title=OU men's basketball: Austin Reaves returns to Wichita a different player than when he left |url=https://oklahoman.com/article/5649877/ou-mens-basketball-austin-reaves-returns-to-wichita-a-different-player-than-when-he-left |website=[[The Oklahoman]] |access-date=November 10, 2020 |date=December 14, 2019}}</ref>

===Oklahoma===
[[File:Austin Reaves Oklahoma (cropped).jpg|thumb|left|150px|Reaves at Oklahoma in 2019]]
After his sophomore season, Reaves transferred to [[Oklahoma Sooners men's basketball|Oklahoma]] and sat out the following season due to [[NCAA]] transfer rules. During his [[redshirt (college sports)|redshirt]] year, he [[Strength training|weight trained]] and gained {{Convert|20|lb|0}}.<ref>{{cite web |last=Buettner |first=Joe |title=OU men's basketball: Austin Reaves makes most of redshirt season in weight room |url=https://www.normantranscript.com/sports/all_ou_sports/ou-mens-basketball-austin-reaves-makes-most-of-redshirt-season-in-weight-room/article_b1ce3c0b-d662-5a24-a06e-659686b21391.html |website=[[The Norman Transcript]] |access-date=November 10, 2020 |date=June 27, 2019}}</ref> On March 7, 2020, Reaves recorded a career-high 41 points, six assists and five rebounds in a 78–76 win over [[2019–20 TCU Horned Frogs men's basketball team|TCU]]. He led a 19-point second-half comeback and made the game-winning shot with 0.5 seconds remaining.<ref name="emig">{{cite web |last=Emig |first=Guerin |title=Putting Austin Reaves' wonder game vs. TCU in perspective |url=https://tulsaworld.com/sports/college/ou/guerin-emig-putting-austin-reaves-wonder-game-vs-tcu-in-perspective/article_9ff7755f-3156-59a3-ab99-0f940d5836c7.html |website=[[Tulsa World]] |access-date=November 10, 2020 |date=March 9, 2020}}</ref> As a redshirt junior, Reaves averaged 14.7 points, 5.3 rebounds and three assists per game and was named to the [[Big 12]] All-Newcomer Team.<ref name=taylor>{{cite web |last=Taylor |first=Erick |title=Still bouncing around: Paths lead brothers back home for now |url=https://www.nwaonline.com/news/2020/may/20/still-bouncing-around-20200520/ |website=[[The Northwest Arkansas Times]] |access-date=November 9, 2020 |date=May 20, 2020}}</ref> On December 6, 2020, he posted a senior season-high 32 points, nine assists and six rebounds in an 82–78 win against [[2020–21 TCU Horned Frogs men's basketball team|TCU]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Hart |first=Hallie |title=OU men's basketball: Austin Reaves scores 32 points to lead Sooners past TCU in Big 12 opener |url=https://www.oklahoman.com/story/sports/college/sooners/2020/12/07/ou-mens-basketball-austin-reaves-scores-32-points-to-lead-sooners-past-tcu-in-big-12-opener/315180007/ |website=[[The Oklahoman]] |access-date=July 28, 2021 |date=December 7, 2020}}</ref> In the second round of the [[2021 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]], Reaves scored 27 points in an 87–71 loss to top-seeded [[2020–21 Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball team|Gonzaga]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Carlson |first=Jenny |title=Carlson: Austin Reaves 'left it all out there' but Sooners can't topple undefeated Gonzaga |url=https://www.oklahoman.com/story/sports/college/basketball/2021/03/22/oklahoma-basketball-austin-reaves-gonzaga-march-madness/4799884001/ |website=[[The Oklahoman]] |access-date=July 28, 2021 |date=March 22, 2021}}</ref> As a senior, he averaged 18.4 points, 5.5 rebounds and 4.6 assists per game, earning first-team [[List of All-Big 12 Conference men's basketball teams|All-Big 12]] honors. On March 31, Reaves declared for the [[2021 NBA draft]], forgoing his remaining college eligibility.<ref>{{cite web |last=Givony |first=Jonathan |title=Oklahoma Sooners guard Austin Reaves declaring for NBA draft |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/31171561 |website=[[ESPN]] |access-date=July 28, 2021 |date=March 31, 2021}}</ref>

==Professional career==
=== 2021–22 season ===
[[File:Austin Reaves (cropped).jpg|thumb|150px|right|Reaves shoots a layup over [[Isaac Okoro]] in 2022.]]
Reaves went [[List of National Basketball Association undrafted players|undrafted]] in the [[2021 NBA draft]]. He said he declined to be selected 42nd overall by the [[Detroit Pistons]],<ref>{{cite web | title=Detroit Pistons wanted to draft Austin Reaves in 2021. He explains why he said no thanks | url=https://www.freep.com/story/sports/nba/pistons/2023/07/20/detroit-pistons-nba-austin-reaves-undrafted-los-angeles-lakers/70437315007/ }}</ref><ref>{{cite video|title=Austin Reaves Ep 192 ALL THE SMOKE Full Episode SHOWTIME BASKETBALL|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vmVhy5O2qZs&t=445s|time=7:25|website=youtube.com|date=July 21, 2023|access-date=July 23, 2023}}</ref> opting instead to sign a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] on August 3, 2021.<ref>{{cite web |last=Kioski |first=Nick |date=August 3, 2021 |title=Lakers Sign Joel Ayayi and Austin Reaves to Two-Way Contracts |url=https://www.nba.com/lakers/releases/lakers-sign-joel-ayayi-austin-reaves-two-way-contracts |access-date=August 3, 2021 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> On September 27, he was signed to a standard NBA contract.<ref>{{cite web |last=Wong |first=S. |date=September 27, 2021 |title=Lakers Sign Austin Reaves to Standard NBA Contract |url=https://www.nba.com/lakers/releases/lakers-sign-austin-reaves-to-standard-nba-contract-2021 |access-date=September 27, 2021 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> On October 22, Reaves made his NBA debut, scoring eight points off the bench in a 115–105 loss to the [[2021–22 Phoenix Suns season|Phoenix Suns]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Suns vs. Lakers - Box Score - October 22, 2021|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/boxscore/_/gameId/401358780|url-status=live|access-date=October 23, 2021|website=ESPN|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211023065615/https://www.espn.com/nba/boxscore/_/gameId/401358780 |archive-date=2021-10-23 }}</ref> On December 15, he scored 15 points, on 5-of-6 shooting from three, grabbed seven rebounds and hit a game-winning three-pointer in a 107–104 victory over the [[2021–22 Dallas Mavericks season|Dallas Mavericks]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/lakers-news-lebron-james-reacts-to-austin-reaves-game-winner-vs-mavs/|title=LeBron James reacts to Austin Reaves' game winner vs. Mavs|website=ClutchPoints|last=Corvo|first=Michael|date=December 16, 2021|access-date=December 17, 2021}}</ref> During the Lakers' season finale on April 10, 2022, in a 146–141 overtime win over the [[2021–22 Denver Nuggets season|Denver Nuggets]], Reaves notched the first [[triple-double]] of his career, and put up career highs in rebounds, and previously assists, with 16 rebounds and 10 assists along with 31 points in 42 minutes.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/nba/2022/04/11/reaves-monk-lead-lakers-past-nuggets-146-141-in-ot/50054629/|title=Reaves, Monk lead Lakers past Nuggets 146-141 in OT|website=USA Today|publisher=Associated Press|date=April 10, 2022|access-date=April 10, 2022}}</ref>

=== 2022–23 season ===
On March 19, 2023, Reaves scored a then-career-high 35 points with six rebounds and six assists off the bench in a 111–105 win against the [[2022–23 Orlando Magic season|Orlando Magic]], in which he scored the final 10 points for the Lakers.<ref>{{cite web|url= https://clutchpoints.com/lakers-news-lebron-james-stunned-reaction-austin-reaves-carrying-la|title= LeBron James' stunned reaction to Austin Reaves carrying Lakers vs. Magic|website=ClutchPoints|last=Salao|first=R.P.|date=March 19, 2023|access-date=March 19, 2023}}</ref> On April 16, in game 1 of the first-round playoff series against the [[2022–23 Memphis Grizzlies season|Memphis Grizzlies]], the first NBA playoff game of his career, he scored 23 points in a 128–112 win. He matched that performance in game 4 of the same series, leading the Lakers in scoring in a 117–111 overtime victory. His successful rookie year led to him receiving the nicknames "Hillbilly Kobe", "White Kobe" and "AR-15", although Reaves himself publicly expressed dislike for such nicknames.<ref>{{Cite web |last=McMenamin |first=Dave |date=July 22, 2022 |title=Lakers' Reaves wants to shed 'AR-15' nickname |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/34280037 |access-date=October 27, 2023 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-07-22 |title=Lakers guard Austin Reaves wants to get rid of 'AR-15' nickname |url=https://www.cbssports.com/nba/news/lakers-guard-austin-reaves-wants-to-get-rid-of-ar-15-nickname/ |access-date=2023-05-23 |website=CBSSports.com |language=en}}</ref>

=== 2023–24 season ===
On July 6, 2023, Reaves re-signed with the [[2023–24 Los Angeles Lakers season|Los Angeles Lakers]] on a four-year, $54 million contract.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-07-06 |title=Los Angeles Lakers Re-Sign Austin Reaves |url=https://www.nba.com/lakers/news/los-angeles-lakers-re-sign-austin-reaves-070623 |access-date=2023-07-06 |website=NBA.com }}</ref><ref name=price_11102023>{{cite news|first=Khobi|last=Price|title=Lakers get healthier, shake up starting lineup in Phoenix|date=November 10, 2023|newspaper=Los Angeles Daily News|url=https://www.dailynews.com/2023/11/10/lakers-get-healthier-shake-up-starting-lineup-in-phoenix/|access-date=November 11, 2023}}</ref> He started the first eight games of the [[2023–24 Los Angeles Lakers season|2023–24 season]] for a streak of 34 consecutive starts, dating back to the 2022–23 regular season and playoffs, before coming off the bench for 15 points and seven assists against the Suns in the Lakers' first road win of the season.<ref name=price_11102023/><ref>{{cite news|first=Khobi|last=Price|title=Lakers rally past Suns for first road win in their In-Season Tournament debut|date=November 10, 2023|newspaper=Los Angeles Daily News|url=https://www.dailynews.com/2023/11/10/lakers-rally-past-suns-for-first-road-win-in-their-in-season-tournament-debut/|access-date=November 11, 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|first=Dan|last=Woike|title=Lakers defeat the Suns for first road win of the season|date=November 10, 2023|newspaper=Los Angeles Times|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/lakers/story/2023-11-10/los-angeles-lakers-phoenix-suns-nba-game-recap|access-date=November 11, 2023}}</ref>

On December 9, 2023, Reaves and the Lakers won the [[2023 NBA In-Season Tournament|inaugural season]] of the [[NBA In-Season Tournament]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |date=2023-12-10 |title=Lakers win in-season tournament final behind Anthony Davis' 41-20 |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/39080368 |access-date=2026-07-23 |website=ESPN.com|last=Bontemps|first=Tim}}</ref> Reaves scored 28 points off the bench in the [[2023 NBA In-Season Tournament championship game|championship game]] against [[2023–24 Indiana Pacers season|Indiana]].<ref name=":0"/>

On January 31, 2024, Reaves put up a then season-high 28 points along with six assists and two steals in a 138–122 loss to the [[2023–24 Atlanta Hawks season|Atlanta Hawks]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-01-31 |title=Lakers' Austin Reaves: Hits for season-high 28 in loss |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/lakers-austin-reaves-hits-for-season-high-28-in-loss/ |access-date=2024-02-04 |website=CBSSports.com |language=en}}</ref> In his next game, on February 1, 2024, he put up 32 points on a career-high seven three-pointers made in a 114–105 win over the [[2023–24 Boston Celtics season|Boston Celtics]].<ref>{{cite web|url= https://clutchpoints.com/lakers-news-austin-reaves-los-angeles-boston-celtics-lebron-james-anthony-davis|title=Austin Reaves sounds off after leading Lakers to huge upset over Celtics without LeBron James, Anthony Davis|website=ClutchPoints|last=Corvo|first=Michael|date=February 1, 2024|access-date=February 2, 2024}}</ref> In his next game on February 3, his first at [[Madison Square Garden]], Reaves provided 22 points, six rebounds, seven assists and two blocks as the Lakers beat the [[2023–24 New York Knicks season|New York Knicks]] 113–105, including four free throws down the stretch.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Austin Reaves Career Vs New York Knicks |url=https://www.statmuse.com/nba/ask/austin-reaves-career-vs-new-york-knicks |access-date=2024-02-04 |website=StatMuse |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Los Angeles Lakers vs New York Knicks Feb 3, 2024 Game Summary |url=https://www.nba.com/game/lal-vs-nyk-0022300701 |access-date=2024-02-04 |website=www.nba.com |language=en}}</ref> Playing without [[LeBron James]] on March 26 against the [[2023–24 Milwaukee Bucks season|Milwaukee Bucks]], Reaves had a triple-double with 29 points, 14 rebounds and 10 assists in a 128–124 road win in double overtime.<ref>{{cite news|first=Dan|last=Woike|title=Lakers open six-game trip with double-overtime win over the Bucks|date=March 26, 2024|newspaper=Los Angeles Times|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/lakers/story/2024-03-26/los-angeles-lakers-milwaukee-bucks-nba-game-recap|access-date=March 27, 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/austin-reaves-insane-triple-double-has-dangelo-russell-lakers-hyped|title=Austin Reaves' insane triple-double has D'Angelo Russell, Lakers hyped|website=ClutchPoints|last=Sampson|first=Peter|date=March 26, 2024|access-date=March 26, 2024}}</ref>

=== 2024–25 season ===
On December 25, 2024, Reaves scored the game-winning layup and finished with a triple-double of 26 points, 10 rebounds and 10 assists in a 115–113 win over the [[2024–25 Golden State Warriors season|Golden State Warriors]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Lakers 115-113 Warriors (Dec 25, 2024) Game Recap |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401704974 |access-date=December 26, 2024 |work=ESPN |date=December 25, 2024 |language=en}}</ref> On December 28, Reaves put up a career-high 16 assists in a 132–122 win over the [[2024–25 Sacramento Kings season|Sacramento Kings]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/lakers-news-austin-reaves-right-mentality-career-high-assists|title=Austin Reaves reveals right mentality amid career-high in assists|website=ClutchPoints|last=Yapkowitz|first=David|date=December 29, 2024|access-date=December 30, 2024}}</ref> On January 17, 2025, Reaves scored a then career-high 38 points in a 102–101 win over the [[2024–25 Brooklyn Nets season|Brooklyn Nets]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/lakers-scrutiny-dangelo-russell-prepared-austin-reaves-la-scrutiny|title=How D'Angelo Russell prepared Austin Reaves for Lakers scrutiny|website=ClutchPoints|last=Yapkowitz|first=David|date=January 18, 2025|access-date=January 18, 2025}}</ref> Reaves later broke this record on February 8, scoring 45 points in a 124–117 win over the [[2024–25 Indiana Pacers season|Indiana Pacers]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401705308|title=Austin Reaves scores a career-high 45, and the Lakers shock the Pacers 124-117 without LeBron, Luka|publisher=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]|date=February 8, 2025|access-date=February 9, 2025}}</ref> With that performance, Reaves became the fourth Laker in the last twenty years to score at least 45 points, joining [[Kobe Bryant]], LeBron James and [[Anthony Davis]]. Further, Reaves is only the sixth Laker ever to score a statline of 45 points, 7 rebounds and 7 assists.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-02-09 |title=Austin Reaves enters hallowed Lakers territory with his 45-point barrage against the Pacers |url=https://apnews.com/article/lakers-austin-reaves-126b05a37ed7ba432b5359b6c8c56d92 |access-date=2025-02-10 |website=AP News |language=en}}</ref>

On April 3, 2025, Reaves had 31 points, 6 rebounds and 3 assists in a game against the Golden State Warriors. Reaves made 9 3-pointers, with a majority of them coming in the 4th quarter. Reaves also passed Lakers great [[Kobe Bryant]] for the second-most three-point field goals in a season in Lakers history.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.si.com/nba/warriors/news/los-angeles-lakers-announce-starting-lineup-vs-warriors-01jqz7gh81b8|title=Austin Reaves Makes Lakers History vs Warriors|last=Esnaashari|first=Farbad|publisher=[[Sports Illustrated]]|quote=According to the Lakers, Reaves moved into second place all-time in Lakers history for three-pointers made in a single season. He surpassed both Nick Van Exel and Kobe Bryant on the list.|date=April 4, 2025|access-date=April 4, 2025}}</ref>

=== 2025–26 season ===
On October 26, 2025, Reaves had a near-triple-double of 51 points, 11 rebounds and 9 assists in a 127–120 win over the [[2025–26 Sacramento Kings season|Sacramento Kings]]. His 51 points set a career high, and he became the eighth Laker to score 20-plus free throws in a single game. He also made his 500th three-pointer of his career.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/46741338|title=Austin Reaves scores career-high 51 points as Lakers top Kings|website=ESPN.com|date=October 27, 2025|access-date=October 27, 2025|last=McMenamin|first=Dave}}</ref> On October 29, Reaves scored a game-winning, buzzer-beating floater and finished with 28 points and a career-high-tying 16 assists in a 116–115 victory against the [[2025–26 Minnesota Timberwolves season|Minnesota Timberwolves]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401809991|title=Lakers fend off Timberwolves on Austin Reaves' buzzer-beater for 116-115 win|publisher=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]|date=October 30, 2025|access-date=October 30, 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/nba/los-angeles-lakers/lakers-news-austin-reaves-timberwolves-comeback-buzzer-beater|title=Lakers' Austin Reaves sinks Timberwolves' comeback bid with crazy buzzer-beater|website=ClutchPoints|last=Finnegan|first=Troy|date=October 29, 2025|access-date=October 29, 2025}}</ref> 

=== 2026–27 season ===
On June 24, 2026, Reaves signed a four-year, $185 million max deal with the Lakers, which made Reaves have the richest contract in NBA history for an undrafted player.<ref>{{cite news |title=Sources: Lakers' Reaves intends to sign 4-year, $185M max deal |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/49166079 |work=[[ESPN]] |date=June 24, 2026 |access-date=June 24, 2026|others=Contributed by Dave McMenamin and Bobby Marks}}</ref>

== National team career ==
Reaves was selected to play on the [[2023 United States FIBA Basketball World Cup team|2023 U.S. national team]] for the [[FIBA Basketball World Cup|FIBA World Cup]]. He was only the third undrafted NBA player on a U.S. national team, following [[Ben Wallace (basketball)|Ben Wallace]] (2002) and [[Brad Miller (basketball)|Brad Miller]] (2006).<ref>{{cite web|first=John|last=Schuhmann|title=USA Basketball taking inexperienced roster to 2023 FIBA World Cup|date=August 3, 2023|website=NBA.com|url=https://www.nba.com/news/usa-basketball-roster-2023-fiba-world-cup|access-date=August 7, 2023}}</ref>

==Off the court==
===Personal life===
Reaves grew up a [[Los Angeles Lakers]] fan.<ref>{{cite web |last=Brown |first=James |title=Austin Reaves reveals the source of his inspiration for his outstanding performance |date=March 20, 2023 |url=https://www.lakerszone.us/lakersnews/Austin-Reaves-reveals-the-source-of-his-inspiration-for-his-outstanding-performance-20230319-0007.html |publisher=Lakers Zone |access-date=20 March 2023}}</ref>

Reaves is the son of Nicole Wilkett and Brian Reaves. Both of his parents played college basketball for [[Arkansas State Red Wolves|Arkansas State]]. His mother averaged 21.3 points per game and earned all-conference honors as a senior, while his father tied for third in program history with 384 career assists.<ref>{{cite web |last=Eldridge |first=Taylor |title=Arkansas State game takes WSU's Austin Reaves back to his roots |url=https://www.kansas.com/sports/college/wichita-state/article190453029.html |website=[[The Kansas City Star]] |access-date=November 9, 2020 |date=December 18, 2017}}</ref> Reaves' brother, Spencer, played college basketball for [[North Greenville Trailblazers|North Greenville]] and [[Central Missouri Mules basketball|Central Missouri]] before embarking on a professional career with [[Iraurgi SB|Juaristi ISB]] in Spain.<ref name=taylor/> As of 2023–24, Spencer is with [[SC Rasta Vechta|Rasta Vechta]] in Germany. Reaves credits his brother for sparking his interest in basketball.<ref>{{cite web |last=Bitterman |first=Abby |title='I might not be here': How Austin Reaves' older brother made the Sooners guard the player he is today |url=https://oklahoman.com/article/5652646/i-might-not-be-here-how-austin-reaves-older-brother-made-the-sooners-guard-the-player-he-is-today |website=[[The Oklahoman]] |access-date=November 9, 2020 |date=January 18, 2020}}</ref>

Reaves' grandmother is German, which allowed him to obtain a German passport in 2022. In 2023, he expressed interest in playing for [[Germany men's national basketball team|Germany's national team]],<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-03-22 |title=Austin Reaves might play for Germany in 2023 FIBA World Cup |url=https://basketnews.com/news-187088-austin-reaves-might-play-for-germany-in-2023-fiba-world-cup.html |access-date=2023-03-23 |website=basketnews.com |language=en}}</ref> but later joined the [[2023 United States FIBA Basketball World Cup team|2023 U.S. World Cup team]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-06-04 |title=USA FIBA Basketball World Cup 2023 roster: Anthony Edwards, Tyrese Haliburton headline commitments to US men's team |url=https://www.sportingnews.com/us/nba/news/team-usa-fiba-basketball-world-cup-2023-roster/iuikgk3hhiplytsuy6bsv8sx |access-date=2023-06-15 |website=sportingnews.com |language=en-us}}</ref>

===Endorsements===
In March 2023, Reaves signed a signature shoe deal with Chinese sports apparel brand Rigorer, whose shoes he wore through the 2022–23 season. The first shoe named "AR1" was released in August 2023 via sneaker marketplace [[Kicks Crew]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Li |first=Nicolaus |date=15 August 2023 |title=Closer Looks: Austin Reaves x Rigorer AR1 "Ice Cream" |url=https://hypebeast.com/2023/8/rigorer-austin-reaves-signature-ar1-ice-cream-closer-look-release-info |website=Hypebeast}}</ref>
